_comment: 工具清单。本仓库不分发任何第三方工具二进制。bootstrap 按本表从各官方源下载到对应分类目录。版本与 official_source 已于 2026-06-29 联网核验(latest_verified/update_available)。下载前仍建议复核官方当前 release。
note_cheat_engine: Cheat Engine 默认不更新、不自动下载,除非用户明确要求。

static-reversing.name: IDA Pro
static-reversing.note: 商业软件,本仓库不下载不分发。**已实测安装并授权**:junction Static-Reversing\IDA -> D:\Software\Tool\Debugger\IDA Professional 9.2,idapro.hexlic 存在,ida.exe + idat.exe 均在。agent 默认走 **idalib**(`D:\Software\Developer\Python314\Scripts\idalib-mcp.exe`)或 `idat -A`,**不是** GUI 13337;13337 仅在人已开 ida.exe 时用(见 OWNER.md:13 / AGENTS.md:123 勿加第二台 IDA 服务)。2026-09-30 实测:idalib-mcp 起 HTTP 8745,66 工具,反编译自建 c01-stringobf 成功。**注意:其失败返回 isError=false + {code:null,error:...},封装必须查 error 字段。**

static-reversing.name: ida-pro-mcp (idalib)
static-reversing.note: pip 包 ida-pro-mcp 2.0.0(mrexodia)+ idapro 0.0.10(Hex-Rays SDK)。启动: `idalib-mcp --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8745 <binary>`;MCP 走 **POST** /mcp(GET 返回 405,是协议不是故障);每次调用需 database=<session_id>。与本文件 third_party 里登记的 stdio+13337 GUI 插件路径是**两条不同路径**,agent 用 idalib。

static-reversing.name: radare2
static-reversing.note: Zip extracts one version folder. r2mcp: `r2pm -Uci r2mcp`.

debuggers.name: GH Injector
debuggers.note: 官方 zip 是注入器库 V4.8,入口是 Symbol Mapper GUI(GH Injector SM - x64.exe),不是 GH Injector.exe。

network-http.name: Wireshark
network-http.note: PAF extracted under portable/. Installer: WiresharkPortable64_4.6.8.paf.exe. Npcap installer is under Npcap-installer.

network-http.name: Npcap
network-http.note: Free installer is GUI-only (/S is OEM). download-tools.ps1 does not run it.

system-forensics.name: Volatility 3
system-forensics.note: 内存镜像取证框架;volatility3-mcp 后端的前置(其 requirements 也会拉取)。win-exes 2.28.0 in _download-stage.

web-reverse.name: web-reverse lab
web-reverse.note: Loopback lab target: HMAC-signed POST /api/submit gate (401 bad/stale, 409 replayed, 200 accepted), readable /plain signer, obfuscated /obf signer (string array + mangled ids + flattened flow), /fingerprint bot-detection surface. Nothing is downloaded.

web-reverse.name: web-reverse capture
web-reverse.needs: Node >= 22 (global WebSocket), Chrome; msedge.exe accepted as fallback
web-reverse.note: Drives a disposable lab Chrome over the devtools websocket: Network.requestWillBeSent + Runtime.addBinding XHR tap + Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument. No npm install. tools/chrome.mjs resolves Chrome first, then msedge.exe, so BOTH are launched by absolute path -- naming the fallback here is what stops a clone from assuming Chrome is the only browser that works.

web-reverse.name: web-reverse recover
web-reverse.note: Deobfuscation: locate string-array indirection, decode it, then verify key candidates by reproducing captured signatures with node:crypto and the server keyId. Reports nothing it did not reproduce.

web-reverse.name: web-reverse replay
web-reverse.note: North-star proof for the JS domain: mint a valid request outside the browser. Verbatim copy must fail, recomputed signature must pass.

web-reverse.name: web-reverse fingerprint
web-reverse.needs: Node >= 22, Chrome; msedge.exe accepted as fallback
web-reverse.note: Bot-detection report: which signals fired, and how many points come from our own CDP instrumentation (--compare runs CDP vs no-CDP baselines). Detector/reporter only - no evasion, no spoofing.

web-reverse.name: web-reverse loop
web-reverse.needs: Node >= 22, Chrome; msedge.exe accepted as fallback
web-reverse.note: One command that runs gate -> capture -> recover -> replay -> fingerprint and judges itself. Exit 0 = loop closed. Wrapper: scripts/web-reverse-lab.ps1

crypto-lab.name: crypto-lab target
crypto-lab.note: Loopback JWT issuer (5 profiles: strong, weak-claims, none, confusion, weak-secret) plus 4 verifiers (strict, confused, none-accepting, naive), each responding with the exact checks it performed. GET /api/health /api/jwks /api/posture. RSA keypair is generated at runtime into crypto-lab/keys/ (gitignored) - no key material in git, HMAC secrets are published fake constants.

crypto-lab.name: crypto-lab analyzer
crypto-lab.note: THE DELIVERABLE. Given a JWS it reports header, every claim with its meaning, expiry status, algorithm family, signature verdict, and which weakness classes are present (unsigned-none, algorithm-confusion, weak-claim-validation, claim-provenance). Findings carry id/severity/class/evidence/why. exit 0 analysed, 2 usage, 3 bad input, 4 --expect mismatch. Never dereferences a jku/x5u key URL.

crypto-lab.name: crypto-lab oracle (node)
crypto-lab.note: Independent implementation #1, used only to cross-check the analyzer. Not committed (crypto-lab/node_modules is gitignored); recreate with `npm install` inside crypto-lab/. Measured: it refuses `alg:none` under a pinned RS256 allowlist ('jwt signature is required') and refuses HS256 keyed on a PEM public key ('secretOrPublicKey must be a symmetric key when using HS256').

crypto-lab.name: crypto-lab oracle (python)
crypto-lab.official_source: https://pypi.org/project/PyJWT/ and https://pypi.org/project/cryptography/ (pip, isolated in crypto-lab/.venv)
crypto-lab.note: Independent implementation #2, different lineage from jsonwebtoken. Not committed (.venv is gitignored); recreate with `python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -r crypto-lab/requirements.txt`. Measured: InvalidKeyError on HS256-with-a-public-key, and PyJWT requires an explicit algorithms allowlist.

crypto-lab.name: crypto-lab loop
crypto-lab.note: Self-judging North Star proof: 12 classification cases (exact finding-id sets), a 5x4 issuer x verifier acceptance matrix, three-implementation agreement, and a live negative control on the --expect guard. Exit 0 = every weakness class was classified as expected. Wrapper: scripts/crypto-lab.ps1 (also scripts/agent-cli.ps1 crypto-lab ...).

forensics-lab.name: forensics-lab scenario
forensics-lab.note: THE GROUND TRUTH, in one file: 8 processes (1 spliced out of the EPROCESS list), 5 VADs (1 injected private RWX PE, 1 PE-shaped READONLY data decoy, 1 load-list-backed image region), 4 sockets, 5 handles, and 3 artifact sets. Frozen clock 2026-03-14T02:17:33Z, no wall-clock and no randomness, so the image is byte-reproducible. External IP 203.0.113.23 is RFC 5737 TEST-NET-3 and the C2 name uses .invalid (RFC 2606) - both are documentation-only and unroutable. Read only by tools/loop.mjs; the analyser never sees it.

forensics-lab.name: forensics-lab payload
forensics-lab.note: The self-authored PE embedded in the injected region, so 'there is a PE here' is checkable by a tool that is not this lab. INNOCUOUS: one exported marker string, no network, no injection, no persistence, no evasion. Built with `lab/payload/build.bat` (cl /LD /O1 /Brepro), verified byte-reproducible across two runs. The DLL is gitignored; without it the lab falls back to lab/mkimage.mjs:buildMinimalPe, a hand-built PE that DieE still calls PE64. No third-party binary is committed.

forensics-lab.name: forensics-lab generator
forensics-lab.note: Writes the D12IMG container: a self-describing header, UTF-16LE string table, region contents, EPROCESS pool blocks with a real doubly-linked ActiveProcessLinks chain, socket chain, VAD chain, handle blocks, and 3 independent artifacts (Amcache-shaped TSV, binary MAM-like .pf files, SRUM-shaped TSV). Fixed-stride records with offsets asserted against the spec on every build. Artifacts land in %TEMP%\d12-forensics-lab, never in the repo.

forensics-lab.name: forensics-lab triage
forensics-lab.note: The instrument. Volatility-equivalent plugins over the image: banners (refuses a file that is not a D12LAB container, and refuses a stride mismatch), pslist (follows ActiveProcessLinks.flink), psscan (sweeps the pool by signature - a different walk, so the two can disagree), malfind (private + executable + structurally valid PE via e_lfanew, minus regions a load-list module backs), netscan, handlescan, plus one parser per artifact format. Every claim carries source, method and tier. Never reads the spec or the fixture's UNLK flag.

forensics-lab.name: forensics-lab analyzer
forensics-lab.note: THE DELIVERABLE, and the triangulation invariant as code: a claim is INFERRED only when >= 2 distinct source GROUPS support it, where a group is an acquisition path (MEM/AM/PF/SRUM), not a file. Five prefetch files are one source; one image read by six plugins is still one source. Tiers OBSERVED/INFERRED/POSSIBLE/REJECTED. The planted decoy is not special-cased: it falls out of the same rule as everything else, so there is no `if (decoy)` anywhere. exit 0 analysed, 3 unreadable target, 4 --expect mismatch.

forensics-lab.name: forensics-lab correlate
forensics-lab.note: Carves the injected region to a real file and hands the bytes to independent implementations: DieE (expects PE64) and YARA-X with a lab rule (expects the marker hit). Also runs a CAPABILITY PROBE against real Volatility 3 and records its refusal verbatim, because 'it cannot consume a synthetic image' is a claim and this is the evidence. States explicitly that tool agreement raises confidence in an OBSERVED value and does NOT add a source group.

forensics-lab.name: forensics-lab loop
forensics-lab.note: Self-judging North Star proof, 37 assertions: determinism, triage, exact findings-set comparison against the ground truth, decoy rejection, the Volatility probe, and FOUR negative controls (A clean image yields no injection finding; B a one-byte tamper removes the finding while an independent one survives; C deleting SRUM demotes the injection to POSSIBLE; D --expect with a wrong set exits 4). Exit 0 = loop closed, 9 = an assertion failed. Wrapper: scripts/forensics-lab.ps1 (also scripts/agent-cli.ps1 forensics-lab ...).

fuzz-lab.name: fuzz-lab corpus
fuzz-lab.note: 27 seeds built from OTHER LABS' deterministic generators (the 5 synthetic pcaps, the 7 binary .pf records + D12IMG + 2 TSV artifacts, 5 signed JOSE tokens, 6 committed JS sources) - never random bytes, because a mutation fuzzer spends its budget on structurally hopeless inputs. Built TWICE per run and the hashes compared, so determinism is measured rather than asserted. That check earned its place: it caught web-reverse/static/gen-obf.mjs being non-deterministic (javascript-obfuscator's internal RNG is not reached by --seed), and those seeds were dropped. Artifacts land in %TEMP%\fuzz-lab, never in the repo.

fuzz-lab.name: fuzz-lab mutator
fuzz-lab.note: 12 NAMED strategies aimed at the fields parsers actually trust: intInject (2/4/8-byte boundary integers over a length or count field, LE and BE), truncate (biased to just past a header boundary - this is the over-read probe), chunk{Delete,Duplicate,Insert,Zero}, byteSplice/alphabetSplice, textRun/textRepeat (the ReDoS probes). xoshiro128** seeded from the run id, so any input is re-derivable. The recipe IS the inverse of the mutation and it round-trips exactly (2400/2400 verified) - recording the step-count draw, the strategy-selection draw and the alphabet VALUES, all three of which were bugs that silently produced wrong bytes.

fuzz-lab.name: fuzz-lab pcap reader
fuzz-lab.note: A libpcap reader, written for the fuzzer because the station had a pcap WRITER (net-reverse/lab/pcap-writer.mjs) and no JS reader - net-reverse shells out to tshark, and a third-party dissector is not a target this repo may claim. Handles all four magics and both byte orders, bounds every declared length against the file, and reports truncation rather than throwing. Ships with a deliberately flawed twin whose defect is SILENT rather than loud: it subarrays incl_len unchecked, and Buffer.subarray clamps, so it returns a 4-byte frame while REPORTING 1000. A crash-counting fuzzer sees nothing there; a differential oracle sees the lie.

fuzz-lab.name: fuzz-lab driver
fuzz-lab.note: One child process per input, for ENFORCEMENT rather than isolation: a regex backtracking through a 400 KB claim never yields to the event loop, so the only way to bound a hang is to kill the process. Hard per-input wall clock (4 s) and a hard V8 heap ceiling (192 MB via --max-old-space-size). Five outcome classes, and the load-bearing distinction is rejected-vs-uncaught: a parser that DECLARES its refusals has handled hostile input correctly, anything else is a finding. worker.mjs deliberately has NO self-abort timer - it could not fire during a synchronous hang, so it would have been a safety net that was dead code.

fuzz-lab.name: fuzz-lab triage
fuzz-lab.note: Delta-debugging minimisation (coarse chunk removal, then byte-wise) against the REAL subprocess with the REAL ceilings - minimising against a cheaper predicate risks reducing to something that only misbehaves in-process, and the reduced case would not reproduce. The reproducer BYTES are written to the gitignored crashes/ dir; the RECIPE (run id, seed hash, strategy chain, reduced hash) is the committed form, and tools/replay.mjs re-derives the bytes and checks the hash. A reproducer is hostile input against parsers this repo ships, so it does not belong in git next to them.

fuzz-lab.name: fuzz-lab loop
fuzz-lab.note: Self-judging North Star proof over 4 targets: corpus stability -> campaign -> triage (every finding reproduced from its recipe, minimised, reduced case re-verified) -> THE NEGATIVE CONTROL -> regressions. Exit 0 is NOT available to a run that found nothing: a surviving flawed twin fails the run, because a fuzzer that cannot catch a parser with no bounds checks has not shown it can catch anything. That check already earned its place - an early run reported the web-triage twin SURVIVED, and the cause was a mutator whose text inputs were too SMALL to trip a quadratic regex. Fixed by widening the strategy, not by weakening the assertion. Exit 0 loop closed, 9 an assertion failed. Wrapper: scripts/fuzz-lab.ps1 (also scripts/agent-cli.ps1 fuzz-lab ...).

ops.name: SkillSpector
ops.note: NVIDIA SkillSpector. Launched UNCONDITIONALLY by headless-lab/tools/skill_security_control.ps1:24 -- that command IS the ops.skill.security negative control, so a clone that cannot run it cannot run the registry at all, which is why this was a real gap and not a cosmetic one. Measured 2026-10-03 on this station: skillspector.exe --version prints 'SkillSpector v2.12.0'. NOT on PATH and NOT in the system Python: it comes from `uv tool install git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector.git`, which lands a self-contained venv plus this launcher, and the bare name `skillspector` does NOT resolve on PyPI. `dir` holds the whole path and there is deliberately no `entry`, following the idalib record above: a host-absolute path is not resolvable relative to the repo, so declaring an `entry` beside it would make every declared-location checker report it absent.

build.name: MSVC vcvars64
build.note: The VC developer environment, not a single tool: four lab builds shell out to vcvars64.bat and then compile with cl/link, so the .bat is the thing a clone must have. crackme-corpus/tools/build-c.ps1:26-30, headless-lab/tools/build.ps1:32-35 and managed-lab/tools/build.ps1:40-43 probe five candidate paths and hard-fail (exit 3, or a throw) when none exists; forensics-lab/lab/payload/build.bat:5 calls one path unconditionally. Measured 2026-10-03 on this station: PRESENT at ...\2022\Community and ...\18\Community, ABSENT at ...\2022\Professional, ...\2022\Enterprise and the x86 BuildTools path. Only forensics-lab/payload had this recorded at all, as the `needs` string 'MSVC 2022 (optional)' on an in-tree entry, which is why three labs were building on a dependency nothing named. `dir` holds the whole path and there is deliberately no `entry`, following the idalib record above.
